Now, I can just sit at my desk for hours, staring at the agenda. I barely speak to my husband or my staff anymore, and I just... I feel almost nothing about the work I used to absolutely love. 

Speaking of my husband, he’s been trying to get me to go to this couples’ tennis clinic at the club. We joined the country club a few years ago mostly for the networking, but the tennis courts are actually stunning. Clay courts, just like at Roland Garros. Have you ever watched the French Open? The way they slide on that clay is incredible. It ruins your shoes, though. I bought these specialized tennis shoes, pristine white, and after one lesson they were completely red. I tried to have the housekeeper clean them—she’s a miracle worker with most things, like that lemon oil I mentioned—but even she couldn't get the red dust out of the mesh. It’s funny how some stains just set in permanently, isn't it? Kind of like red wine on a white rug. We had this gorgeous Persian rug in our old apartment in the city, and during a holiday party, someone—I still don't know who—spilled an entire glass of Cabernet on it. You can't just use club soda on a hand-woven silk rug. You have to call in these specialists who take it away for weeks and charge an absolute fortune...

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Something about the club? Or my husband?

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response:
Depressed? No, I wouldn't say I've been depressed. I mean, I'm not crying all day or anything like that. I just... I don't know, I just don't have the energy I used to. Like I said, I just sit there. 

But depressed... no. My sister, though, she gets depressed. She has this light box she sits in front of every winter because she says the lack of sun in Seattle just ruins her mood. Seattle is so gloomy, isn't it? It rains constantly. I went there for a tech conference a few years ago—we were looking into upgrading our entire server infrastructure—and it literally drizzled for five days straight. The coffee is amazing, though. We went to the original Starbucks at Pike Place Market, but honestly, the line was out the door, so we ended up at this tiny little independent roaster down the street. They did this pour-over Ethiopian blend that had these incredible blueberry notes. I bought a bag of the beans to take home, but I never got around to buying a proper burr grinder. You really need a burr grinder, not a blade grinder, if you want a consistent extraction. Blade grinders just chop the beans into uneven pieces, and then your coffee tastes bitter. My husband tried to use it for spices once, actually, which was a disaster because then the coffee tasted like cumin for a month. Cumin is such an overpowering flavor...

I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. Were you asking about my sister's light box?
